Contributing to sysPrep

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution to sysPrep. This package formalizes preprocessing methods for NSSP ESSENCE syndromic surveillance data, so changes are held to a high bar for correctness and for stability: people run these functions inside production surveillance pipelines, and a change that quietly alters output is costly even when it is well meant.

This guide is short on purpose. If something here is unclear, open an issue and ask.

Never post real data

sysPrep handles surveillance records. Do not post patient-level data, identifiable facility information, or anything covered by a data use agreement in an issue, pull request, or discussion. That includes screenshots and copied console output.

Reproduce problems with the built-in synthetic datasets (essence_raw, essence_clean, essence_ed_raw, essence_inp_raw) or with a few invented rows. If you accidentally post sensitive data, contact the maintainer right away (see SECURITY.md) so it can be removed.

Reporting a bug or suggesting a feature

Please use the issue forms. The most useful reports include:

  • a minimal reproducible example built from synthetic data (the reprex package helps),
  • the ESSENCE data source the pull came from (va_er, va_hosp, or other),
  • the output of sessionInfo(), including the sysPrep version.

If a function behaves differently at your site (a different duplication mechanism, different facility types, different Region formats), use the “Site or data source behavior” form. Those reports are especially valuable because the package was developed against a limited set of sites.

For a non-trivial change, open an issue before writing code so we can agree on the approach. It saves you from doing work that conflicts with the design contract below.

Design contract

These are the rules the package follows. A pull request that breaks one is likely to be asked to change.

  1. Existing output must not change silently. Changing what a function returns for valid input is a behavior change. It needs an issue, an entry in NEWS.md, and a stated reason. Prefer adding an optional argument whose default keeps the current behavior.
  2. Inform, warn, abort, in that order of severity. Use rlang::inform() for expected, actionable messages, rlang::warn() for unexpected but non-fatal conditions, and rlang::abort() only when continuing would produce silently wrong results. Every function that has a verbose argument must silence all of its messages with verbose = FALSE (warnings still show).
  3. clean_names is optional. Functions normalize names internally so that column arguments accept raw ESSENCE names (HospitalName) or snake_case (hospital_name). With clean_names = FALSE they must return the caller’s own column names.
  4. Identifiers are text. Linking keys such as Hospital, Visit_ID, and C_BioSense_ID have no numeric meaning and are compared as text.
  5. A missing key is an unknown identity, not a match. Rows with a missing facility_col or visit_col are never merged with each other.
  6. HasBeen_ flags are always 0 or 1. Never NA. A flag that is 1 on either side of a linked encounter stays 1.
  7. No real data anywhere in the package. Example data and tests use synthetic records only.

Development setup

# install.packages(c("devtools", "testthat", "roxygen2", "lintr", "covr"))
devtools::load_all()     # load the package from source
devtools::test()         # run the test suite
devtools::document()     # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE after editing roxygen
devtools::check()        # R CMD check; aim for 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes

The package requires dplyr >= 1.2.0.

Pull request checklist

Code style

  • Follow the tidyverse style guide. Lines are at most 80 characters (enforced by .lintr).
  • Use the native pipe |>, rlang::abort()/warn()/inform() with call = rlang::caller_env() so errors name the function the user called, and rlang::arg_match() for choice arguments.
  • Keep exported functions short: put each stage in a documented internal helper.
  • Write prose without em dashes; use commas, colons, or semicolons.
  • Wrap code, argument, and field names in backticks in documentation.

Code of conduct

Please note that this project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing, you agree to abide by its terms.
